Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Health Partners Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during the call. Today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Health Partners' financial results for the third quarter. Joining me on the call are David Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; John Reynolds, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Emily Carter, Chief Medical Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Operating Officer; and Lisa Patel, Chief Innovation Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to David Reynolds.

David Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on six key aspects: Trends in inpatient vs. outpatient volumes, Breakdown of revenue by service line, Trends in staffing levels and contract labor usage, Labor costs as a percentage of revenue, Supply costs and other operating expenses, and Overview of key financial performance highlights.

In terms of trends in inpatient versus outpatient volumes, we saw continued strength in outpatient growth amid some inpatient softness, reflecting industry shifts toward ambulatory care. Revenue breakdown showed robust gains in outpatient services, while staffing trends improved with lower contract reliance. Labor costs held steady as a share of revenue, supply expenses were well-managed, and overall financial highlights demonstrated solid growth and margin expansion.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to John Reynolds to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

John Reynolds:
Thank you, David. Good morning, everyone. As David mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Net revenue for the third quarter was $2.85 billion, an increase of 7.2% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, favorable payer mix, and the successful implementation of our revenue cycle management initiatives.

Our operating expenses were $2.32 billion, representing 81.5% of net revenue. We are continuing to focus on managing our costs effectively while investing in key growth initiatives, particularly in ambulatory expansion.

Net income for the quarter was $285 million, or $1.45 per share. We are pleased with our financial performance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial goals for the year.

Let me unpack these results further, starting with an overview of our key financial performance highlights. As a leading operator of acute care hospitals, ambulatory surgery centers, and post-acute facilities across 15 states, we delivered robust top-line growth and margin expansion in the quarter ended September 30, 2024. Consolidated net revenues hit a record $2.82 billion, up 9.2% year-over-year from $2.58 billion. This was powered by a 6.8% rise in patient service revenues, with inpatient admissions at 142,000, up 4.5%, and our case mix index climbing to 1.92, a 2.1% improvement from higher-acuity procedures in orthopedics and cardiology. Outpatient volumes surged 12.7% to 1.8 million encounters, led by a 28% revenue jump in our ASCs from demand for cataracts, joint replacements, and GI endoscopies.

Payer mix stayed favorable, with commercial and managed care at 52%, Medicare at 38%, and Medicaid at 8%. Net revenue per admission increased 3.4% to $18,200, aided by a 3.6% IPPS base update and strong payer contracts with UnitedHealthcare and Blue Cross affiliates. Adjusted EBITDA reached $512 million at an 18.2% margin, up 110 basis points, as operating expenses fell to 81.8% of revenue. Supply costs grew just 4.2%, labor at 52% expanded only 5.1% via retention efforts and AI scheduling in 70% of facilities. Operating cash flow hit $620 million, up 22%, funding $180 million in CapEx for ASCs and ORs. We ended with $1.2 billion in liquidity, 2.8x leverage, and returned $75 million to shareholders.

Southeast markets, with 55% of beds, grew 11% from Florida and Texas tailwinds, Midwest 8% via a new Ohio ASC, while Northeast faced 2% pressure offset by 22% telehealth outpatient growth. Our Outpatient First strategy shifted 65% of procedures to ASCs, boosting margins 300 basis points, with 40% Medicare lives in ACO REACH yielding $45 million in savings. Revenue cycle improvements cut A/R to 45 days, adding $30 million in cash. We're raising full-year EBITDA guidance to $2.05-$2.10 billion.

Diving deeper into trends in inpatient versus outpatient volumes, these continue shaping our revenue mix and margins, driven by value-based care, site-neutral payments, and ambulatory tech advances. Across our 45 acute care hospitals, 120 outpatient centers, and 30 ASCs in 12 states, same-facility outpatient grew 8.2% year-over-year, managing inpatient pressures. Total visits hit 2.8 million, up 6.1%. Inpatient admissions were 112,000, down 1.8% same-facility, ADC at 18,200 beds off 0.9%, adjusted patient days at 1.45 million down 2.1%. CMI steady at 1.92, with complex oncology and cardiac at 28% of revenue, up from 24%.

Outpatient encounters jumped 12.4% to 2.65 million, ASC and HOPD procedures up 15.2%, observation stays up 9.8% to 45,000. This mirrors HCA and Tenet trends, with net revenue per adjusted patient day up 4.2% to $2,450.

Inpatient headwinds include procedure migration—CMS OPPS shifted 12 procedures to ASCs, like knee arthroscopies now 35% inpatient versus 70% in 2021. MA penetration at 42% shortened LOS to 4.7 days, with 18% elective ortho denials. Commercial bundled payments compressed pneumonia DRGs by 1.5%. Seasonally, flu/RSV down 5%, offset by 22% COVID uptick. Nurse ratios improved to 1:4.2, but 8% below pre-pandemic in some areas.

Outpatient acceleration to 68% of visits, up from 62%, outpaced 7-9% benchmarks. New ASCs in Phoenix, Orlando, Dallas added 12 ORs at 85% utilization, capturing 65% HOPD cases. Cataract surgeries up 18%, ASC margins at 25%. Epic MyChart cut no-shows to 12%, da Vinci in 15 ASCs boosted hysterectomies 31%, telehealth up 28% to 320,000 converting 42% to procedures. Ancillaries like infusions and PSMA PET grew 14%.

Sunbelt flat inpatient, 16% outpatient; Midwest balanced; Northeast softest at -4.2% inpatient. We're investing $450 million CapEx for 20 ASC ORs, divested rural sites for $120 million into JVs, guiding Q4 outpatient 10-12% up, inpatient down 1-2%, total revenue 7-8%, CMI to 1.94. This drove 12.5% EBITDA margins.

On breakdown of revenue by service line, total net patient service revenue was $2.85 billion, up 7.2% year-over-year and 2.1% sequentially, our 11th straight growth quarter, from 4.5% EPD increase and 2.8% CMI to 1.92. Across 52 hospitals, 28 ASCs, 15 behavioral sites, and practices in 14 states, Sunbelt at 62%.

Inpatient acute: 42% or $1.20 billion, +3.1%, from 2.8% admissions to 128,000, ADC up 3.2% to 18,400, LOS to 4.7. Payer mix 48% Medicare, 32% managed Medicaid, 18% commercial. Margins to 22.4% despite 6% nurse costs, offset by Vanguard Optimizer cutting agency 22%.

Outpatient: 38% or $1.08 billion, +14.6%, 18% procedures to 245,000 led by ortho +22% with Mako, GI +16%. Revenue per case $4,400, Texas +21%. Margins to 34.1%, 60% of $450 million CapEx. Tele-outpatient via Epic up 35%.

ED: 11% or $314 million, +1.2%, flat 1.05 million visits, CMI 1.15 from stroke/sepsis. Rapid Triage AI cut times 18%, margins 18.2%.

Physician/ancillaries: 6% or $171 million, +9.8%, radiology +12%, labs +11%, home health +15% Florida.

Behavioral: 3% or $86 million, +8.4%, IOP/PHP +10% from opioids, adding 200 Phoenix beds.

Outpatient share up from 32%, ratio 1.1:1 inpatient-to-outpatient. Sunbelt 12% growth, divesting PA hospitals. Epic unlocked $45 million productivity, MSSP ACO $28 million savings. Q4 guide 8-10% growth, outpatient 16-18%.

Turning to trends in staffing levels and contract labor usage, across our 42-hospital Southeast/Midwest footprint, nursing FTEs at 28,500, up 2.2% sequentially, 4.8% year-over-year, supporting 6.1% adjusted patient days, 3.8% ADC. Non-clinical up 1.5% to 12,200 via Epic and centralized RCM. RNs 42% of clinical FTEs, turnover 14.2% from 22%, LPN/CNA stable at 9.8%/8.4%.

Contract labor 12.4% of nursing hours, down from 18.7%, $145 million or 420 bps pressure, labor at 52.3% versus 55.1% last year. Conversion rate 68%, Heroes program with $25,000 sign-ons, $5,000 stipends, 1,200 conversions saving $42 million annualized, agency $120/hour vs. $68 internal.

Sunbelt 15.2% contract from growth/vacancies 18%; Midwest 8.9% via float pools. LeanTaaS iQueue cut overstaffing 11%, overtime 17%; Qventus pilots for 20-25% cut; Teladoc offloaded 14% visits, saving 450 FTEs.

Pillars: Horizon Academy 850 RNs at 92% retention; $180 million wages with 5.8% merits; M&A like Dayton 200-bed. Q4 contract to 11.5%, labor 51.5%. Risks CMS minimums, but positioned for 8-10% contract, 200-300 bps EBITDA.

Labor costs as a percentage of revenue hit 56.8%, up 120 bps year-over-year but flat sequentially, on $1.42 billion up 8.2% with FTEs to 78,500, revenue $2.50 billion up 6.9%. Wage inflation 5.8%, RNs 7.2% on 4.8% vacancy from 6% national. Contract 7.5% of hours at 45% premium, overtime from 9% CMI uptick, benefits +6.4%.

Coastal 62.3% from mandates/unions, Midwest 53.2%, Sunbelt 55.1%. Turnover to 14.2% below 16.8% benchmark. Optimization: Epic AI scheduling accuracy 92% cut overtime 22%; Nuance scribing freed 1.2 FTEs/100 beds; residencies 2,500 grads; LPN-RN bridges 18% fills; outpatient 58% cut intensity 25%; telehealth +35%; Vizient GPO 2.1% admin savings; Accenture RCM $40 million.

Q3 trough 56.5%, Q4 55.8%, better than HCA 55.2%, Tenet 57.9%. With 2.7% IPPS boost, to mid-teens margins by 2026.

Finally, supply costs and other operating expenses at 28% of op ex, 18% revenue. Supplies $285 million, +4.1%, 12.4% revenue down 40 bps. Procedural volumes up, but med-surg inflation 5.8% on gloves/sutures 15-20% above 2021. Pharma +2.9% to $92 million via 340B +15 sites $18 million discounts; GLP-1 +25% countered by step therapy. Implants/devices $118 million +6.2% from ortho/robotics, Vizient 8-10% better terms. Northeast higher, Midwest lower. Inflation cooled 3.5%, on-time 94%.

Initiatives: Palantir AIP cut stockouts 22%; ASC shift 20% lower costs; value analysis 7% savings. Other op ex $412 million +3.2%, 15.6% revenue: fees +4.5% locums/telehealth, UKG cut agency 18%; facilities +2.8% utilities, LEED 12% HVAC savings; IT +6% Epic/cyber. Sunbelt lowest intensity.

Q3 supplies 12.3-12.6%, other mid-single growth. Targeting $150 million savings by 2025 via GPO/RFID/Medtronic. Drove 250 bps margin to 14.2%.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Emily Carter for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Emily Carter:
Thank you, John. Good morning. We are making significant progress in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our bundled payments for care improvement program has shown promising results, with a 25% reduction in readmission rates. We are also focused on leveraging technology to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination, specifically through our telehealth platform, which now handles 22% of outpatient visits and supports seamless virtual care integration with Epic.

Following that, Michael Chen will provide an update on operational efficiency.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Dr. Carter. We are focused on streamlining our operations and improving efficiency across our network. We have implemented several initiatives, including LeanTaaS iQueue for AI-driven predictive staffing and centralized revenue cycle management with AI denial prediction, which have resulted in significant cost savings, including reduced overtime by 17% and A/R days to 45.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Lisa Patel for an overview of our innovation efforts.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Michael. We are committed to driving innovation across our organization. We are investing in new technologies and partnerships to improve patient care, enhance efficiency, and create new revenue streams. Our current projects include AI-powered diagnostics for early detection in oncology and next-generation robotics like da Vinci 5 systems, which directly address healthcare challenges such as staffing shortages and procedure migration by enabling same-day discharges and reducing readmissions by 15%.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to David Reynolds.

David Reynolds:
Thank you, Lisa. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the specific cost savings achieved through the implementation of LeanTaaS iQueue?

Michael Chen:
Absolutely, John. The LeanTaaS iQueue deployment across 85% of our facilities has leveraged AI predictive analytics to align staffing precisely with census fluctuations, delivering an 11% reduction in overstaffing and 17% cut in overtime year-to-date. In high-volume Sunbelt markets, it's covered 22% of shifts via internal float pools, bringing contract dependency down to 11.5% projected for Q4 and contributing over $42 million in annualized savings from fewer agency hours. Combined with our Horizon Academy pipeline, it's a cornerstone of our margin expansion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mary Johnson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mary Johnson:
What are your expectations for the impact of telehealth on your revenue and patient access?

Dr. Emily Carter:
Great question, Mary. Telehealth has been transformative, with volumes up 28-35% year-over-year to over 320,000 encounters, converting 42% to in-person procedures and shielding us from billing disputes under the No Surprises Act. It enhances access, particularly in rural extensions of our footprint, offloading 14% of routine visits and easing RN demands equivalent to 450 FTEs. Revenue-wise, it drives ancillary uplift like imaging follow-ups at 14% growth, and we expect it to contribute 2-3% to total revenue growth in 2025 as Epic MyChart integration hits 95%, while cutting no-shows to 12% and supporting outpatient margins at 34%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Bob Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Bob Lee:
Can you provide more details on your plans for investing in new technologies and partnerships?

Lisa Patel:
Sure, Bob. Our $450 million CapEx allocates 60% to tech and ambulatory innovation, including Palantir Foundry for supply AI reducing stockouts 22%, Qventus for workforce cuts of 20-25%, and partnerships like Teladoc for telehealth, Vizient for GPO leverage yielding 7-10% savings, and JVs with SCA Health and Boston Scientific for ASC ramps. Robotics like da Vinci in 15 sites and GE AI scanners boost ortho and radiology 12-22%, targeting 72% outpatient mix by 2026. M&A dry powder at $1.2 billion focuses tuck-ins in stable markets, echoing HCA's model for 10-12% growth.

Operator:
Thank you for the questions. This concludes the question-and-answer session.

David Reynolds:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the Apex Health Partners Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
